report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Fixed 9-month deadline and $850k budget force predictive scheduling; evolving integration scope and plugin architecture require adaptive backlog refinement within phases.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Build an internal developer platform (IDP) providing unified service discovery, self-serve infrastructure provisioning, onboarding automation, and incident management for 200-person engineering org across 12 product + 3 platform squads.
project_understanding.beneficiary: Engineering organization (product + platform squads); primary users: squad leads, platform engineers, on-call engineers.
project_understanding.trigger: No unified developer experience today; 140 microservices + 340 repos scattered across GitHub, AWS, PagerDuty, Jira; onboarding manual; incident response fragmented.
success_definition: Service catalogue auto-discovers all repos with owner, SLOs, dependencies, deploy history, runbooks; search p95 < 1.5s
Self-serve provisioning (Postgres, Redis, S3, SQS, ECS) with Terraform + approval workflow + cost estimate
Onboarding checklist auto-provisions GitHub, IAM, Slack, Jira for new squads
Incident view aggregates PagerDuty alerts with service metadata (owner, deploys, deps, runbook)
Plugin system (REST + webhooks) supports security scans, DORA metrics, custom integrations
99.9% uptime; squad-level RBAC for cost/provisioning; 2-year audit log for all provision actions
supporting_quotes: Build an internal developer platform (IDP) for a 200-person engineering org
Service catalogue (auto-discover repos; owner, SLOs, deps, deploys, runbooks; search)
Self-serve provisioning (Postgres, Redis, S3, SQS, ECS) via Terraform + approval + cost estimate
Integrations (must support): GitHub, AWS, Terraform Cloud, PagerDuty, Jira, Confluence, Slack, Okta SSO, Datadog
9 months to first internal full launch; $850k budget

assumption_log.what: Security review and compliance audit (SOC 2 / data handling) will be completed within Phase 3 and do not require external vendor approval beyond internal security team.
assumption_log.why: IDP handles IAM, cost data, and audit logs; security review is standard for internal platforms. No external compliance body mentioned (not HIPAA/PCI). Assuming internal security team capacity exists.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 — Risk identification before planning baseline; security is a material NFR.
assumption_log.consequence: If external compliance audit required (e.g., SOC 2 Type II), Phase 3 extends 4–6 weeks; budget impact ~$30–50k for audit firm.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows Phase 3 to proceed without external dependency. Risks: if wrong, schedule slips and budget overruns.

assumption_log.what: Terraform Cloud API and AWS IAM/ECS/RDS/S3/SQS/CloudWatch APIs are fully documented, sandbox-accessible, and stable (no breaking changes during 9-month build).
assumption_log.why: These are mature, vendor-supported APIs. Assuming no undocumented endpoints or schema drift. Sandbox access is standard for AWS and Terraform Cloud.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 — Integration risk identification; external API stability is a known failure mode.
assumption_log.consequence: If API schema changes or sandbox access delayed, Phase 2 development blocked for 2–4 weeks; integration testing (Phase 3) extends.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows development to proceed without API discovery delays. Risks: if wrong, critical path slips.

assumption_log.what: PagerDuty, Jira, Confluence, Slack, and Okta SSO provide REST APIs with webhook support and do not require custom authentication beyond standard OAuth/API keys.
assumption_log.why: All are SaaS platforms with documented public APIs. Assuming no custom authentication or approval process beyond standard API key provisioning.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 — Integration risk; external SaaS API availability and stability.
assumption_log.consequence: If any SaaS API requires custom authentication or has undocumented rate limits, Phase 2 integration work extends 1–2 weeks per API.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows parallel integration development. Risks: if wrong, integration testing (Phase 3) becomes sequential bottleneck.

assumption_log.what: Plugin system (REST + webhooks) will use a standard webhook delivery model (HTTP POST with retry logic) and does not require custom message queue or event streaming infrastructure beyond what AWS SQS provides.
assumption_log.why: REST + webhooks is a standard pattern for extensibility. Assuming no need for Kafka, RabbitMQ, or custom event bus. SQS is already in the provisioning scope.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 — Scope baseline; plugin architecture is a known design pattern.
assumption_log.consequence: If plugin system requires custom event streaming (Kafka), Phase 2 architecture extends 2–3 weeks; infrastructure cost increases ~$5–10k/year.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: simplifies Phase 2 architecture; uses existing AWS services. Risks: if wrong, plugin performance or reliability may require re-architecture.

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Backend developers (4 total) must be dedicated to critical path tasks (service catalogue, provisioning engine, integrations); FE and UX can work in parallel on UI with 2–3 day slack. DevOps/platform engineer is critical path for infrastructure setup and Phase 5 deployment.

risk_register.description: If AWS IAM, ECS, RDS, S3, SQS APIs have undocumented endpoints, rate limits, or schema drift during build, integration testing (Phase 3) will be blocked for 2–4 weeks and critical path slips.
risk_register.trigger: API documentation gaps discovered during Phase 2 development; rate limit errors in staging; schema changes from AWS
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm sandbox access and API stability with AWS account team in Phase 1; subscribe to AWS API change notifications; build rate limit handling into all AWS clients
risk_register.contingency: If API issues discovered, allocate 1 backend developer full-time to AWS integration troubleshooting; extend Phase 3 by 2 weeks if needed

risk_register.description: If Terraform Cloud, PagerDuty, Jira, Slack, or Okta APIs require custom authentication, have undocumented rate limits, or webhook delivery is unreliable, Phase 2 integration work extends 1–2 weeks per API.
risk_register.trigger: API documentation gaps; webhook delivery failures in staging; rate limit errors; custom auth requirements
risk_register.mitigation: Validate API contracts with each vendor in Phase 1; test webhook delivery in sandbox before Phase 2 development; build retry logic and exponential backoff into all integrations
risk_register.contingency: If webhook delivery unreliable, implement custom polling fallback; if rate limits hit, implement request queuing (SQS)

risk_register.description: If service catalogue search does not meet p95 < 1.5s NFR with 340 repos, database indexing or search algorithm must be re-architected in Phase 3, delaying integration testing by 1–2 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Performance testing in Phase 3 shows p95 > 2s; database query plans show full table scans
risk_register.mitigation: Design database indexes in Phase 1; implement search index (Elasticsearch or PostgreSQL full-text search) in Phase 2; performance test early in Phase 2 with 340 repos
risk_register.contingency: If p95 > 1.5s, implement Elasticsearch or Redis caching; re-run performance tests; adjust Phase 3 timeline

risk_register.description: If any of the 4 backend developers are diverted to other projects or unavailable part-time, critical path tasks (AWS integration, provisioning engine, plugin system, audit logging) will slip 2–4 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Developer pulled to production incident; competing project priority; unplanned leave
risk_register.mitigation: Secure written commitment from engineering leadership for 4 full-time backend developers for 9 months; establish escalation path if diversion occurs; cross-train 2 developers on each critical component
risk_register.contingency: If developer unavailable, hire contractor backend developer (2–4 week ramp-up); extend timeline by 2 weeks per diverted developer

risk_register.description: If Phase 1 architecture or API contracts are not finalized by week 4, Phase 2 development will start with ambiguous requirements, causing rework and 2–3 week delay.
risk_register.trigger: Architecture workshop delayed; stakeholder sign-off not obtained; API contracts incomplete
risk_register.mitigation: Schedule architecture workshop in week 1; require stakeholder sign-off by end of week 3; document all API contracts before Phase 2 starts
risk_register.contingency: If Phase 1 extends, compress Phase 2 by reducing edge case handling; defer non-critical integrations (Datadog) to post-launch

risk_register.description: If stakeholders request features beyond MVP (e.g., cost chargeback, advanced RBAC, custom workflows) during Phase 2, scope creep will consume 2–4 weeks of development time.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder requests new feature; PM adds to backlog without re-planning; feature not in original MVP scope
risk_register.mitigation: Define MVP scope in Phase 1 and get written sign-off; establish change control process; defer all non-MVP features to Phase 2 (post-launch)
risk_register.contingency: If scope creep occurs, prioritize features by impact; defer lowest-priority features to post-launch; re-baseline timeline with stakeholders

risk_register.description: If security review in Phase 3 identifies critical findings (e.g., RBAC bypass, audit log gaps, SSO token handling), remediation will extend Phase 3 by 1–2 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Security review finds critical vulnerability; RBAC enforcement incomplete; audit log missing actions
risk_register.mitigation: Involve security engineer in Phase 1 architecture; implement RBAC and audit logging in Phase 2 (not Phase 3); conduct security review early in Phase 3
risk_register.contingency: If critical findings, allocate security engineer + 1 backend developer full-time to remediation; extend Phase 3 by 1–2 weeks

risk_register.description: If UX designer or frontend developers are shared with other projects, UI development (Phases 2–4) will be delayed or incomplete, impacting user adoption.
risk_register.trigger: UX designer allocated < 60% to IDP; frontend developers pulled to other projects; UI design not completed by end of Phase 1
risk_register.mitigation: Secure written commitment for 1 full-time UX designer (Phases 1–2) and 2 full-time frontend developers (Phases 2–4); establish escalation path if diversion occurs
risk_register.contingency: If UX designer unavailable, use wireframes from Phase 1 as design spec; if frontend developers diverted, hire contractor frontend developer

risk_register.description: If infrastructure costs (PostgreSQL, Redis, S3, ECS, monitoring) exceed $850k budget or 12-month estimate, project will be over budget by $50–100k.
risk_register.trigger: AWS cost estimate > $100k/year; Datadog pricing higher than expected; infrastructure scaling required
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct detailed AWS cost estimation in Phase 1; use cost estimation tools (AWS Pricing Calculator); implement cost monitoring in Phase 2; set budget alerts
risk_register.contingency: If costs exceed budget, optimize infrastructure (smaller RDS instance, reduce Datadog retention); defer non-critical features; request budget increase

risk_register.description: If plugin system (REST + webhooks) does not scale to 10+ concurrent plugins or webhook delivery becomes unreliable under load, Phase 3 performance testing will fail and architecture must be re-designed.
risk_register.trigger: Performance testing shows webhook delivery failures; plugin registration API times out; SQS queue backs up
risk_register.mitigation: Design plugin system with SQS queue for webhook delivery in Phase 2; performance test with 10+ mock plugins in Phase 3; implement monitoring and alerting
risk_register.contingency: If webhook delivery unreliable, implement Kafka or RabbitMQ for event streaming; re-architect plugin system; extend Phase 3 by 1–2 weeks

risk_register.description: If GitHub API rate limiting (60 req/min) is hit during catalogue sync, service discovery will be incomplete or delayed, impacting catalogue accuracy.
risk_register.trigger: Catalogue sync fails due to rate limiting; 340 repos not synced; sync takes > 30 minutes
risk_register.mitigation: Implement exponential backoff and request queuing in Phase 2; use GitHub GraphQL API (higher rate limit); sync incrementally (only changed repos)
risk_register.contingency: If rate limiting persists, implement caching (Redis) and longer sync intervals; request GitHub API rate limit increase

risk_register.description: If 9-month deadline is fixed and any critical path task (AWS integration, provisioning engine, plugin system, audit logging) slips by 2+ weeks, project will miss launch date.
risk_register.trigger: Critical path task delayed; developer unavailable; API integration blocked; performance testing fails
risk_register.mitigation: Track critical path weekly; identify risks early; allocate buffer (15% already applied); escalate delays immediately; have contingency plan (defer non-critical features)
risk_register.contingency: If critical path slips, defer non-critical features (Datadog, advanced RBAC) to Phase 2; compress Phase 4 (UAT) to 4 weeks; extend Phase 5 if needed

staffing_plan.notes: Leads architecture workshop (Phase 1), manages scope and stakeholder alignment (all phases), writes documentation (Phase 4), conducts operational handoff (Phase 5)
Front-loaded to Phase 1; leads architecture workshop; defines schema and API contracts

4 backend developers required; split across service catalogue (T7), AWS integration (T8), provisioning engine (T9), onboarding (T10), incident view (T11), plugin system (T12), Okta SSO (T17), audit logging (T18), bug fixes (T28). Each developer owns 1–2 integrations; cross-training required for critical path coverage.
2 frontend developers; build catalogue UI (T13), provisioning UI (T14), onboarding UI (T15), incident view UI (T16); can work in parallel with backend; 2–3 day slack allows flexibility
Front-loaded to Phase 1 (wireframes); Phase 2 (design review); Phase 4 (accessibility audit); can be shared with other projects after Phase 2

1 QA engineer; critical path for integration testing (Phase 3) and UAT (Phase 4); tests all 8 integrations, performance, RBAC, audit log; 25% of total dev hours (280h × 25% = 70h minimum; 124h allocated exceeds minimum)
1 DevOps engineer; sets up dev/staging infrastructure (Phase 2), deploys to production (Phase 5), configures monitoring and alerting; critical path for infrastructure readiness
1 security engineer; defines RBAC model (Phase 1), conducts security review (Phase 3), verifies audit logging (Phase 4); can be shared with other projects
0.5 data engineer (shared); implements Datadog integration (T25) in Phase 3; critical path for DORA metrics feature

open_questions.question: Has written commitment been obtained from engineering leadership confirming 4 full-time backend developers, 2 full-time frontend developers, 1 full-time DevOps engineer, and 1 full-time QA engineer for the full 9-month duration with no diversion to other projects?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If developers are shared or part-time, critical path tasks (AWS integration, provisioning engine, plugin system) will slip 2–4 weeks; project will miss 9-month deadline.

open_questions.question: Can AWS sandbox environment (with IAM, ECS, RDS, S3, SQS, CloudWatch access) be provisioned in Phase 1 for integration development and testing?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If sandbox access delayed, Phase 2 AWS integration development (T8) will be blocked; critical path slips 2–4 weeks.

open_questions.question: Has the $850k budget been formally approved and allocated, and does it include 12 months of infrastructure costs (PostgreSQL, Redis, S3, ECS, Datadog, monitoring)?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If budget is insufficient or infrastructure costs exceed estimate, project will be over budget by $50–100k; may require scope reduction or timeline extension.

open_questions.question: Who is the Product Owner responsible for backlog prioritization and feature trade-offs during Phase 2–3 (Hybrid SDLC requires active PO for sprint planning)?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If PO not assigned, sprint planning will be delayed; backlog prioritization will be unclear; scope creep risk increases.

open_questions.question: Are there any compliance or regulatory requirements (SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, FedRAMP) beyond the stated 2-year audit log and squad-level RBAC that must be implemented before launch?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If compliance requirements discovered post-Phase 1, security review (Phase 3) will extend 2–4 weeks; project may miss deadline.

deductions.reason: 4 assumptions logged (A1–A4); each represents unvalidated risk in API stability, security scope, or plugin architecture
Resource risk (R4): developer diversion not explicitly ruled out in writing; team composition stated but no formal commitment letter mentioned
Scope risk (R6): HIGH probability of scope creep from stakeholders; 15 integrations + plugin system + DORA metrics create feature factory risk

Integration complexity: 8 mandatory integrations (GitHub, AWS, Terraform, PagerDuty, Jira, Slack, Okta, Datadog) + plugin system; Phase 3 is 23% of timeline (typical for TYPE_A is 20–25%, but integration risk is elevated)
SDLC is Hybrid (not Predictive): fixed deadline + evolving integration scope requires active backlog management; PO not named in input
Performance NFR (p95 < 1.5s search) is ambitious for 340 repos; if not met in Phase 3, re-architecture required (R3: MEDIUM score)

pm_confidence_score.interpretation: PM confidence score is 62.0 because the project has a well-defined MVP scope, experienced team composition, and fixed deadline, but is offset by 8 HIGH-scored risks (resource diversion, scope creep, integration complexity, performance targets), 4 assumptions on API stability and security scope, and Hybrid SDLC requiring active backlog management without a named Product Owner.
